subject: COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md entry D-012 — DR-104: component identity, namespace and collision policy (DRAFT — UNDER ADVERSARIAL REVIEW)
protocol: D-000 adversarial review, turn 1 of 3 (reviewer side). Mandate: refute, not confirm.
verdictSummary: 5 MUST-FIX, 3 SHOULD-FIX, 1 NOTE. The entry's two load-bearing citations both fail at their pinned bytes: the PROJECT-ID-V1 citation collapses on the caller-may-not-supply fork (ADV-D012-T1-01), and the 'flat namespace ... is the prototype's model' claim in the Alternatives cell is false at commit a62509d6, where the rejected scoped `opensip <component> <verb>` shape is what the prototype actually ships (ADV-D012-T1-02). The alias-duration borrow cites a window DR-111 is not even commissioned to produce (ADV-D012-T1-03). No objection contests the policy's direction — stable IDs, deny-by-default, typed refusal are all well-grounded; every objection is that the entry specifies less than its citations claim, or claims sources it contradicts.

objections.claim: Clause 1's identity rule is incoherent on the single most load-bearing question — who mints the ID — and the PROJECT-ID-V1 citation collapses on either resolution. The clause specifies the shape the corpus records as the DEFECT (single-record identity, no allocation rule) under the name of the pattern that repairs it.
objections.evidence: PROJECT-ID-V1's recorded strength (IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §3 TM row, line 391, live digest 93a4f74f…): 'ProjectId is total, injective, collision-free, and — verified — a persisted CSPRNG allocation never derived from mutable state'; 'PROJECT-ID-V1 is collision-safe because its identity carries two custody records — marker and registry — with a uniqueness constraint between them, and callers may not supply it; rootId carried one.' The corpus's own lesson is that identity WITHOUT the allocation rule and dual-custody uniqueness constraint (rootId) was the defect. D-012 clause 1 specifies: stable, immutable, 'assigned at first admission', never derived from mutable state, never reused — no allocation rule, no custody/uniqueness constraint, no caller-may-not-supply. Now the fork: (a) if the ID is host-minted at first admission (the PROJECT-ID-V1 reading of 'assigned at first admission'), it contradicts the pinned prototype evidence — packages/core/src/tools/manifest.ts at a62509d6 (sha256 e0f47e6f…) declares 'stableId: Stable machine identity (real UUID) for this tool ... Declared additively by tools that opt into durable identity (first-party tools declare it)' — i.e. AUTHOR-DECLARED in the manifest, existing before any admission — and contradicts file 02's packaging contract (1811c682…, §Common component packaging: the component release emits 'a canonical closed manifest and stable component/release identity'), and breaks portability: the same signed component admitted on two machines would carry two different IDs, while file 02's catalog/lock/signed-release model requires one. (b) if the manifest supplies the ID, then callers DO supply it, and the cited pattern's core property — 'callers may not supply it', stated in the TM row as the very reason it is collision-safe — is the one property the policy inverts. Either way the citation overstates: the lane's fidelity standard (D-007 turn-1's five dropped source elements, all MUST-FIX; D-008 turn-2 SF restoring 'full source fidelity') treats borrowing a corpus pattern's name at less than its recorded strength as a defect. The parenthetical's narrowing ('identity separate from location/name') does not cure it, because the clause simultaneously borrows the pattern's allocation language ('never derived from mutable state') verbatim.
objections.proposedFix: Decide the minting authority explicitly. If publisher-declared (the prototype's and file 02's model): cite the prototype's stableId/manifest-identity evidence — NOT PROJECT-ID-V1 — and supply the property that makes 'never reused' enforceable without host minting: a registry uniqueness constraint at admission binding ID to signed publisher provenance (the dual-custody lesson translated, not name-borrowed), with the ID↔provenance collision a typed refusal. If host-minted: state the per-install consequence, reconcile with file 02's release-identity contract by a reviewed edit, and only then may the PROJECT-ID-V1 citation stand at strength (allocation rule, caller-may-not-supply, dual custody all stated). A third lawful path: keep the clause and demote the citation to 'identity/name separation only, allocation rule differs — see prototype stableId', recorded as a deliberate departure.

objections.claim: The Alternatives cell's factual ground — 'a flat namespace with typed refusal is auditable and the prototype's model' — is false at the pinned bytes. The prototype is flat only at the ROOT; beneath each component primary it is hierarchical, i.e. exactly the scoped `opensip <component> <verb>` shape the cell rejects as not-the-prototype's-model. And the entry never says who owns sub-command grammar below an admitted top-level name — the precise subject of the pinned host-grammar rule.
objections.evidence: opensip-cli at the pinned commit a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0 (HEAD verified equal to pin, clean tree). AGENTS.md (5d2c312b…) CLI bootstrap flow: tools mount 'declarative commandSpecs through the host-owned mountCommandSpec infrastructure. Tools never receive a raw Commander program'; subcommands out of the box include 'opensip fit list', 'opensip fit recipes'; and the host 'mounts a domain-bound plugin group UNDER each pack-supporting tool primary (opensip fit plugin …, opensip sim plugin …) — there is no top-level opensip plugin command.' reject-host-command-collisions.ts (2e454c8f…) checks each spec's root name, root alias, OR PARENT — CommandSpec has a `parent` field; the grammar is a tree. The pinned evidence row itself (prototype-evidence-reference.md 69a71aac…, row 1) names the surface 'Host CLI grammar and MOUNTED TOOL COMMANDS' with semantics 'manifest discovery never hands a component raw ROOT parser authority' — the qualifier 'raw root' exists precisely because components DO receive non-root, host-mediated grammar under their mount. D-012 decides 'single flat top-level namespace' and stops: sub-command grammar ownership (declarative host-mounted specs vs component-owned parsing) is undecided and unmentioned, though slice 1's TypeScript provider is a component (D-006 clause 5) and file 02 (1811c682…) line 79 assigns the host only 'root grammar, flags, collisions, dispatch'.
objections.proposedFix: Restate clause 2 as two decisions instead of one: (i) the ROOT namespace is host-owned, flat, and shared (host + admitted components) — which IS the prototype's root model; (ii) below an admitted top-level name, sub-command grammar is declarative, manifest-declared, and host-mounted — a component never receives raw parser authority at any level (the pinned rule generalized, not just quoted). Re-record the alternatives honestly: the scoped `opensip <component> <verb>` shape is not a rejected alternative — at the pin it is the prototype's own shape for multi-command tools and is COMPATIBLE with (i)+(ii); what was actually rejected is per-component TOP-LEVEL namespace partitioning (every component name auto-prefixed), and that rejection should be argued on its own merits, not on a false prototype attribution.

objections.claim: Clause 3's alias-duration borrow — '(DR-111's surface windows govern duration)' — is a D-010-class citation of an undefined rule, and worse: the cited row is not even commissioned to produce the rule. DR-111 is OPEN, and its own surface enumeration does not contain a CLI command-name/alias surface, so no lawful DR-111 closure will ever yield the window this clause binds to.
objections.evidence: Register file 08 (54e75a33…) line 274: DR-111 status OPEN — 'Separate compatibility windows for core/index/control, each provider major, component API, state schema, and evidence formats.' Its source, file 04 §Separate compatibility matrices (a74b4511…, lines 168-184, read in full — the absence claim is measured on the enumerated list, not inferred from a failed search): eight surfaces — distribution core and core state; signed root/index/manifest/lock schemas; common control protocol; TypeScript provider protocol major 1; Rust merged provider protocol major 2; each other component role API/subprotocol; component-owned state schema; evidence/custody/replay formats. None is the user-facing command-name/alias surface, and the matrices DR-111 must set are 'read/write/migration/refusal' matrices, not deprecation durations. The lane's precedent is exact: D-010 turn-1 MF struck a rule 'defined nowhere' and cured it by reference-with-reopen; D-012 instead binds a product obligation ('at least one compatibility window') to a unit that does not and will not exist. Note the inversion: DR-104's own acceptance cell says 'PRODUCT-APPROVED namespace and migration rules' — the alias window is exactly the number this preference-laden entry exists to decide, and it is the one number the entry declines to decide.
objections.proposedFix: Either (a) D-012 states its own floor in defined units (e.g. 'a deprecated alias survives at least N minor releases of the distribution core, and never less than one', product-decided here), with an explicit supersession clause: 'if a DR-111 closure later defines a command-surface window, that window governs and this floor is superseded by reference'; or (b) a separate reviewed register-content act (the D-010/D-011 pattern: row edit + file 04 §Separate compatibility matrices amended through the register's own process, so text and register never disagree) adds the command/alias surface to DR-111's enumeration, and D-012's citation becomes a lawful forward reference with a reopen clause. As written it is neither.

objections.claim: The reservation set is undefined for the names that matter most: host-owned commands are never admitted, so 'first-party commands reserve their names at admission' reserves nothing for them, and the typed-refusal rule has no defined set to collide against. The pinned prototype solved exactly this gap with machinery D-012 drops entirely.
objections.evidence: Slice-1 host commands (D-002: analyze, doctor, --help/--version) and file 02's management-core surface (1811c682…, §Management core: help, version, completion, configuration, component inventory/lifecycle, status, doctor, repair) are host-owned — they pass through no admission, so under D-012's text no act ever reserves them. The pinned prototype at a62509d6: reserved-names.ts (b08f1d59…) — 'Host-reserved root command names (ADR-0159). Every host-owned root command (visible or internal) plus Commander's implicit help. A Tool whose command specs claim one of these as a root name, root alias, or parent is rejected at admission ... before Commander mounting, so the host surface can never be shadowed or double-mounted. This list is static so the admission gate needs no mounted program; the parity test ... asserts it equals the actually-mounted host surface (names + aliases), so adding or renaming a host command without updating this list fails CI.' Four properties D-012 omits: (1) a-priori static host reservation, not at-admission; (2) coverage of aliases and internal/hidden names (__tool-command-worker etc.); (3) collision checked against name, alias, AND parent claims (a component claiming `doctor` as a PARENT would silently graft onto a host command — D-012's shadow rule covers alias-vs-live-name only); (4) a parity obligation keeping the reserved list equal to the mounted surface.
objections.proposedFix: Add a host-reservation clause: host command names, their aliases, and internal command names are reserved a priori in a host-owned static set; admission collision is evaluated against the union of that set and previously admitted names, over each spec's name, aliases, and parent; a parity check (the reserved set equals the actually-mounted host surface) is named negative-test evidence alongside the collision/cycle/shadow/stale-alias cases.

objections.claim: Clause 4's premise misquotes D-002 — 'slice 1 is first-party-only (D-002)' — dropping the explicitly-trusted class, and the 'transfer reduces to registry bookkeeping' conclusion rests on the dropped half. The deferral naming is also inconsistent with the entry's own routing: namespace DEPTH is routed to the DR-117 successor while ownership transfer/dispute — the same third-party governance surface — is routed to DR-116/DR-010 with DR-117 omitted.
objections.evidence: D-002 Components (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at start digest 5674b446…): 'first-party/explicitly-trusted only (DR-128's MVP boundary)'. DR-128's row (file 08, 54e75a33…): 'MVP permits first-party/explicitly trusted components with DR-G21 fault containment only.' An explicitly-trusted component authored by an external publisher is admissible in slice 1; name custody and ownership between the host and that publisher is not 'first-party bookkeeping', and the row element DR-104 names — 'ownership governance' — has no rule for it and no named deferral covering it (the entry's deferral covers only 'third-party transfer/dispute'). On routing: DR-116 (file 08 line 279) is 'Third-party publisher/support/vulnerability/revocation policy' (Product security); catalog governance depth is DR-117 item 1 ('marketplace/catalog and governance depth' — the enumeration D-011 just count-pinned at seven, file 02 §product boundary at 1811c682…) riding DR-010 ('catalog/lifecycle depth, contribution ontology'). D-012's own Alternatives cell routes hierarchy to 'the DR-117 successor when third-party depth exists', while clause 4 defers transfer/dispute to 'the DR-116/DR-010 successor' — two halves of one surface, two different owner sets, one entry.
objections.proposedFix: Correct the premise to D-002's actual boundary ('first-party/explicitly-trusted'). Scope the bookkeeping reduction to components whose publisher is the product itself; for explicitly-trusted external components give the ownership question either a slice-1 rule (e.g. admission binds name custody to the signed publisher provenance; transfer requires re-admission under the new publisher's signature — consistent with clause 1's fix in T1-01) or its own named deferral. Name the transfer/dispute deferral to DR-010/DR-117 (governance/catalog depth) with DR-116 carrying the publisher-trust/revocation half, so the entry's two third-party routings agree.

objections.claim: The collision universe is incomplete: the policy decides different-components-one-name (refuse) but is silent on one-component-multiple-install-scopes, where the pinned evidence documents DELIBERATE ordering precedence — and clause 2's blanket 'never ... ordering-dependent resolution', read literally, forbids the prototype's project-pin lesson. The Alternatives cell's evidentiary claim is also measurably false: the corpus's admission evidence does not 'forbid order-dependent behavior' — the pinned prototype is order-dependent in two distinct recorded places — and 'silent last-wins' is a straw man no source proposes, while the actually-shipped shape (scoped first-wins) goes unrecorded.
objections.evidence: register-tools-discovery.ts at the pin (0429929b…), buildToolDiscoverySources doc: 'Order is precedence (first-occurrence-wins on duplicate name): 1. project-local .runtime/plugins/tool 2. project tree 3. user-global 4. CLI install dir. A project-local pin therefore SHADOWS a user-global install of the same tool.' registry.ts (f1e6dce4…): 'Duplicate-id policy: first writer wins ... duplicatePolicy: warn-first-wins'. Neither is the straw-man last-wins, and both are ordering-dependent by documented design. The DR-G21 citation in the Alternatives cell is a stretch besides: DR-G21's subject (file 02 §Independent failure containment) is crash/timeout/resource containment, not name resolution; the real anti-collision sources are the prototype's deny-by-default admission row and file 02 line 79 ('The host owns ... collisions'). Distinguish three cases: (i) two different components claiming one name → typed refusal (decided, and a lawful STRENGTHENING of the pin's warn-first-wins — but it should be recorded as a departure from the pinned bytes, not as the pin's mandate); (ii) the same component ID present at multiple install scopes → scope-precedence question, undecided and unmentioned, where refusal would regress the project-pin lesson; (iii) component vs host-reserved name → T1-04.
objections.proposedFix: Add the scope-precedence case: same component ID at multiple install scopes resolves by fixed scope precedence (project > user > system, or as decided) — deterministic by SCOPE, never by discovery order within a scope — and is not a collision; different IDs claiming one name remain a typed refusal regardless of scope. Re-record the alternatives: replace 'silent last-wins' with the pin's actual warn-first-wins/scope-shadowing shape, rejected in favor of typed refusal WITH the scope-precedence carve-out, and drop or correct the DR-G21 citation.

objections.claim: The version half of the pinned admission semantics — 'stable IDs distinct from VERSIONS/aliases' — is quoted in the entry's bound but addressed nowhere in the policy, and the negative-test enumeration omits file 05's version/coexistence goldens, which are DR-104's own recorded acceptance target.
objections.evidence: Prototype-evidence-reference.md (69a71aac…) row 6: 'stable IDs distinct from versions/aliases'. File 02 (1811c682…) §Common component packaging: 'stable component/RELEASE identity' — two identities, component and release; D-012 clause 1 specifies only the component ID and never states the cross-release rule (ID constant across releases; release identity separate; two live releases of one component share one ID and one namespace entry). File 05 (1a57c9ca…) line 92 assigns DR-104 the acceptance target 'rename/alias/VERSION/COEXISTENCE goldens'; D-012 clause 5's negative-test list is 'collision, cycle, shadow, stale-alias' — the version and coexistence cases are absent. The lane's cure for enumeration drift is boundary-by-reference (D-011).
objections.proposedFix: Add the version-distinctness sentence to clause 1 (component ID constant across releases; release identity a distinct field; version never participates in name resolution) and extend clause 5's test enumeration to cover file 05's full set — by count-pinned reference to file 05's DR-104 lesson row, per the D-011 pattern, so the two lists cannot drift.

objections.claim: The file-08 annotation overstates: 'policy DECIDED (D-012)' while the entry itself defers third-party transfer/dispute, scopes the namespace shape to slice 1, and (as drafted) leaves alias duration to an OPEN row. The lane's own precedent annotates what remains undecided.
objections.evidence: D-007 moved DR-118 to DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED with the annotation 'PER-ROW THRESHOLDS REMAIN UNDECIDED' precisely to keep the label honest; D-009's annotation carries the turn-2 rider. D-012's proposed annotation — 'policy DECIDED (D-012); negative-test evidence at qualification' — names no residual, though the entry's own clauses 2 ('for slice 1'), 3 (duration external) and 4 (explicit deferral) each leave one.
objections.proposedFix: Annotate the residuals in the row edit: 'slice-1 namespace/identity policy DECIDED (D-012); third-party transfer/dispute DEFERRED (per T1-06's owner set); alias-window floor per D-012 pending any DR-111 command-surface window; negative-test evidence at qualification.'

objections.claim: The entry's bounding quote truncates the pinned admission semantics: 'no implicit execution during discovery' — the fourth element of the row D-012 quotes — is dropped, and the policy nowhere states that reservation/collision detection is computable from authenticated metadata alone.
objections.evidence: Prototype-evidence-reference.md (69a71aac…) row 6 semantics: 'Manifest-first, deny-by-default, stable IDs distinct from versions/aliases; NO IMPLICIT EXECUTION DURING DISCOVERY.' D-012's preamble quotes the first three. File 02 (1811c682…) lines 76-78: help/completion/inventory 'read authenticated metadata only. They do not execute component code...'; the prototype's reserved list is 'static so the admission gate needs no mounted program' and the manifest is inspectable 'without importing the runtime module' (manifest.ts, e0f47e6f…). The omission is consequential to this policy because name reservation happens at admission: a reservation that required executing the component would violate the dropped element.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the fourth element to the bounding quote and add one sentence: name reservation and collision detection are computed from authenticated manifest metadata only; executing component code during discovery/admission is itself a refusal condition, with a negative test named alongside the others.
